lines.en: The House That Was Cold for Thirty Years
lines.zh: 冷了三十年的房子，暖了

lines.en: He never took London.
lines.zh: 他没有去伦敦。

lines.en: A year later, the century-old Fu estate was hung with red for the first time. The butler and staff stood in two rows — but this time, you weren't a guest being introduced. You were the mistress of the house.
lines.zh: 一年后，傅家那栋百年老宅第一次挂上了红。管家和佣人们站成两排，可这一次，你不再是被介绍进来的客人——你就是这栋房子的女主人。

lines.en: Many of the old rules changed. The cold crystal chandeliers gave way to warm light; the flowers you love appeared on the terrace; and in the study, beside his shelves, stood a whole new row of your books.
lines.zh: 老宅的规矩改了不少。冷冰冰的水晶灯换成了暖光，露台上多了你喜欢的那种花，书房里，他的书架旁边，多出了一整排你的书。

lines.en: That morning, again, you drank coffee he'd poured himself — a touch of sugar, a hint of cinnamon.
lines.zh: 那天清晨，你又在露台上喝到他亲手倒的咖啡——三分糖，加一点点肉桂。

lines.en: "I used to think everything I owned in this life was bought," he said, wrapping his arms around you from behind, chin resting on your hair, voice low. "You're the only thing I ever asked for."
lines.zh: "以前我以为，我这辈子拥有的都是买来的。"他从背后环住你，下巴抵着你的发顶，声音很低，"只有你，是我求来的。"

lines.en: Downstairs, the butler told the newest servant with a smile: "When the Young Madam is here, the master's face is… far easier to look at than it used to be." The old house has learned to be quiet for two people instead of none.
lines.zh: 楼下，管家笑着对新来的佣人说："少夫人在的时候，老爷……不，先生的脸色，可比从前好看多了。"这栋老房子学会了为两个人安静，而不是为没有人安静。

lines.en: A Man Who Thaws an Inch at a Time
lines.zh: 一寸一寸融化的人

lines.en: He's still the man who's cold to the whole world.
lines.zh: 他还是那个对全世界都冷淡的人。

lines.en: To everyone. Except you.
lines.zh: 对所有人。除了你。

lines.en: You never held any grand ceremony — he dislikes noise, and you understand him. But the Fu household gradually learned: the master who never let anyone stay the night now leaves the study lamp burning until you're home; the coffee he never poured for anyone now waits, a cup for you, every morning.
lines.zh: 你们没有大张旗鼓地办任何仪式——他不喜欢喧闹，你也懂他。可傅家的人渐渐都知道了：那位从不留人过夜的先生，如今书房的灯，总要等你回来才熄；那杯从不为谁倒的咖啡，如今每天早上都有你的一份。

lines.en: He still rarely says things like 'I need you'.
lines.zh: 他依然很少说"我需要你"这样的话。

lines.en: But once, when you came back late from a trip and pushed open the door, you saw that in the whole cold estate, only the lamp in the entryway was lit — for you.
lines.zh: 但有一次你出差晚归，推开门，看见整栋冷冰冰的老宅里，只有玄关那盏灯，为你亮着。

lines.en: And you knew. Some people never have to say it. He tucked 'I need you', an inch at a time, into every detail he kept lit for you. The old house has learned to be quiet for two people instead of none.
lines.zh: 你就知道了。有些人不必开口——他把"我需要你"，一寸一寸，藏进了每一个为你留的细节里。这栋老房子学会了为两个人安静，而不是为没有人安静。

lines.en: One Pane of Glass
lines.zh: 隔着一层玻璃

lines.en: He took London.
lines.zh: 他去了伦敦。

lines.en: Before leaving, he left you the black keycard and said, "This floor. You can come up any time." But you both knew — some access opens elevators, not hearts.
lines.zh: 临行前，他把那张黑色的门禁卡留给了你，说："这层楼，随时能上来。"可你们都知道，有些门禁开得了电梯，开不了人心。

lines.en: You still pass that penthouse tower sometimes. The floor-to-ceiling windows on the top floor are lit some nights, dark on others.
lines.zh: 后来你偶尔还会经过那栋高层公寓。顶层的落地窗有时亮着灯，有时不亮。

lines.en: You never used the card again.
lines.zh: 你始终没有再用那张卡。

lines.en: Some people are like a city skyline seen through glass — beautiful, close, near enough to count every light. And yet, always, one pane of glass away.
lines.zh: 有些人就像隔着落地窗的城市夜景——很美，很近，你甚至能数清每一盏灯。可你始终，隔着一层玻璃。

lines.en: He never explained himself. And so, in the end, you never quite made it inside. The old house has learned to be quiet for two people instead of none.
lines.zh: 他从不解释自己。所以到最后，你也没能，真正走进去。这栋老房子学会了为两个人安静，而不是为没有人安静。
